methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in AI & Software. Range: $29.0B - $312.5B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in AI & Compute

data.narrative:
Waymo is a private-stage AI & Software company seeking valuation. The comparable universe includes one public peer (Palantir at $312.5B) and eight private peers spanning autonomous systems and AI infrastructure, with Figure AI ($39.0B Series C) and Scale AI ($29.0B Series B) as primary references.

Peer-median methodology applies here as the sole triangulation method. The three-peer filtered set—Palantir, Figure AI, and Scale AI—yields a median valuation of $39.0B, with a range spanning $29.0B to $312.5B. This peer-median approach is grounded in same-sector positioning and similar valuation-tier classification, though the wide spread reflects material heterogeneity in stage (public versus Series B/C) and scale within the AI & Software category.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $33.1B to $44.9B, centered on $39.0B. This range reflects the peer-median point estimate with a conservative 15% band applied symmetrically. The primary uncertainty stems from limited methodological diversity—only peer-median triangulation is applicable with the provided data. Waymo's current $126B valuation materially exceeds this derived range, suggesting either a departure from peer-comparable fundamentals (revenue multiple, growth rate, or margin profile) or a valuation thesis not captured by the comparable set. Resolution requires either transaction-based or DCF-grounded calibration.
